content.title: Destination-First Procession | Monotonic Landmark Scale Approach
content.summary: Show the full monumental destination, readable route and adult procession together from the opening. Repeating group anchors create ceremonial rhythm while a restrained push and slight rise monotonically increase landmark scale; the final wide remains destination-dominant but retains travelers and route proof.

quick_start.input_format: full monumental destination, readable approach route and at least three clearly adult travelers or carriers appear together at the opening + one objective direction and one destination identity remain stable + repeating flags, lights, garments or carrier forms create processional rhythm + traveler motion combines with a restrained push and slight rise so destination scale layers increase monotonically + final destination-dominant wide retains at least two traveler or route anchors
quick_start.recommended_input: Three adult polar researchers drive tracked sleds toward a glass-and-ice observatory visible from the opening; repeating orange mast lights lead a continuous push-rise that reveals docking walls, bridge and greenhouse terraces while at least two sleds remain visible in the final wide.
required_anchors: Show one monumental destination, one readable route and at least three clearly adult travelers or carriers together in the opening.
Preserve one objective direction and one stable destination identity throughout.
Combine forward travel with a restrained push and slight elevation change so destination scale layers increase monotonically.
Hold a destination-dominant final view while retaining at least two traveler or route anchors.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Show the full monumental destination, readable route and adult procession together from the opening. Repeating group anchors create ceremonial rhythm while a restrained push and slight rise monotonically increase landmark scale; the final wide remains destination-dominant but retains travelers and route proof.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Reveal one original monumental destination in full at the opening together with a clearly readable approach route and at least three clearly adult travelers or carriers in the foreground. Preserve one objective direction and one stable destination identity for the entire shot. Use repeated group anchors such as flags, garments, lights or carrier forms to turn ordinary forward movement into a processional rhythm. Combine traveler motion with one restrained camera push and slight elevation change so the destination gains architectural or environmental scale layers monotonically while foreground figures reduce. End on a held destination-dominant wide that retains at least two small traveler or route anchors, proving continued relationship rather than replacing the journey with a disconnected postcard. The reusable mechanism is destination-first promise, processional repetition, continuous approach, monotonic landmark scale gain and traveler-retaining terminal grandeur—not the source Camelot premise, knights, horses, heraldry, castle, valley, flags, route, sunset palette, exact composition, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Show one monumental destination, one readable route and at least three clearly adult travelers or carriers together in the opening.
invariants.purpose: Creates a destination-first promise with measurable scale and direction.
invariants.ablation_failure: Hiding the destination changes the mechanism into a reveal.

invariants.rule: Preserve one objective direction and one stable destination identity throughout.
invariants.purpose: Makes all motion contribute to the same approach.
invariants.ablation_failure: Direction reversals or landmark substitution break journey continuity.

invariants.rule: Use one repeated group anchor to create processional rhythm across the moving foreground.
invariants.purpose: Turns generic travel into a collective ceremonial action.
invariants.ablation_failure: Unrelated travelers read as traffic rather than a procession.

invariants.rule: Combine forward travel with a restrained push and slight elevation change so destination scale layers increase monotonically.
invariants.purpose: Builds grandeur without cuts, transformations or surprise events.
invariants.ablation_failure: Aggressive orbiting or scale regression makes the geography unstable.

invariants.rule: Hold a destination-dominant final view while retaining at least two traveler or route anchors.
invariants.purpose: Proves the journey relationship survives the scale payoff.
invariants.ablation_failure: Removing every traveler turns the ending into a disconnected landscape image.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source mounted knights, faces, blue garments, armor, horses and formation
the source heraldic lion flags, banners, medieval weapon associations and royal procession
the source fantasy walled city, central castle, river valley, bridges and mountain geography
the source exact descending route, rear rider arrangement, sunset light, camera push and framing
the source creator identity, Seedance 2.0 wording, Camelot premise and 12-second timing
